James De Mille, A Strange Manuscript Found in a Copper Cylinder.
Standard Ebooks edition: https://standardebooks.org/ebooks/james-de-mille/a-strange-manuscript-found-in-a-copper-cylinder

People whose words are in the text, and their death years:
- James De Mille, the author, died 1880 (Wikidata Q1680258, P570 = 1880-01-28).

First publication of the text used: 1888 (SE colophon: 'A Strange Manuscript Found in a Copper Cylinder was published in 1888 by James De Mille.'). The Wikipedia article says the text was first published in nineteen installments in Harper's Weekly, from January 7 to May 12, 1888, and then in book form by Harper & Brothers.

Why this is public domain:
- United States: the text was first published in 1888, before 1931, so the US rule settles its origin too. A published work enters the United States public domain 95 years after publication, so this work entered it in 1983.
- Country of origin (United States): the first publication was the Harper's Weekly serial, a United States magazine, in 1888, before 1931, so the US rule settles the origin, whatever the death year (1880).

The edition's own statement of rights (from the repository's content.opf):
"The source text and artwork in this ebook are believed to be in the United States public domain; that is, they are believed to be free of copyright restrictions in the United States. They may still be copyrighted in other countries, so users located outside of the United States must check their local laws before using this ebook. The creators of, and contributors to, this ebook dedicate their contributions to the worldwide public domain via the terms in the [CC0 1.0 Universal Public Domain Dedication](https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/)."
